title: Repository-Scale Refactoring with Qwen3-Coder
business: Enterprise software teams managing massive legacy codebases
problem: Developers struggle to maintain consistency across large repositories because standard models lack the context window to understand cross-file dependencies, leading to broken builds during refactoring.
solution: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct provides native support for 256K tokens, allowing the model to ingest entire repository structures to perform informed, agentic refactoring tasks.
steps: Initialize the model using AutoModelForCausalLM with device_map set to auto to handle the 30.5B parameter footprint.
Define specific tool functions for file system operations to enable agentic interaction with the codebase.
Load the repository context into the model's 256K token window to ensure global awareness of dependencies.
Invoke the model via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint to execute refactoring commands using the defined tool schema.
Validate the generated code changes against the repository's existing unit test suite.
outcome: Improved code consistency and reduced manual effort in navigating complex, multi-file architectural changes.
limitation: The model requires significant VRAM because all expert weights must reside in memory; if you encounter out-of-memory (OOM) issues, consider reducing the context length to a shorter value, such as 32,768.
